newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan paper says pro-Khartoum forces take towns.
newsitem.headline: Sudan paper says pro-Khartoum forces take towns.

text.p: A Sudanese newspaper said on Thursday that a militia allied with Sudan's government had recaptured two southern towns from rebels.

The private Alwan newspaper said the Southern Sudan Defence Force (SSDF) on Tuesday retook Warap and Tali, more than 960 km (600 miles) south of the capital Khartoum. It gave no source for the report.
The Islamist government in April signed a peace accord with a number of factions now allied in the SSDF.
Alwan also said the SSDF had attacked rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) forces in Duk Fadiat and Duk Faiwil areas, about 840 km (520 miles) south of the capital.
For 14 years the government has been fighting the SPLA, which wants greater autonomy or independence for the mostly Christian and animist south from the Moslem, Arabised north.
